quotes.text: Artificial intelligence is another important issue. A lot of people feel a sense of fear about it. Some people feel a sense of promise and hope about it. There's a needle to thread there where we are ensuring that America is on the cutting edge of this seismic technology but also ensuring that we're protecting American workers, we're protecting our kids' online safety.

I applaud President Trump's announced AI framework. I am confident that under President Trump’s leadership and guided by his America First vision, we will lead the world in artificial intelligence while protecting our most important resource: the American people. 

I share the perspective expressed by Vice President JD Vance. We should not approach AI through a lens of fear, but through a lens of opportunity. 

America must win the race for innovation against China. Today's announcement helps put us on the right track to do this. Thank you, President Trump!

It's clear that the United States is locked in a race with China for leadership in AI, similar to the space race we had against the Soviets in the 1960s, but with potentially much more at stake. This competition between rival nations will shape economic power, national security, and global influence for centuries to come.

Whenever we are talking about the future of AI, we must realize that there are legitimate concerns about workforce displacement that must be addressed, just as there are reasonable guardrails that must be considered. [...] I don't believe we should take a gloom-and-doom view of AI, but I do understand the concerns that others have.

We can't win the AI race without building the needed infrastructure here at home. That means investing in and utilizing the American workforce to build it, oversee it, and ensure the technology companies we use to create that infrastructure do so while respecting the principles of free speech, innovation, and our shared American values.

That's why I strongly support skilled job training that teaches workers how to use AI to enhance their work — not replace it. We should establish a strong baseline of education and training so American workers become more productive, more competitive, and never obsolete.

In my latest @DC_Reporter op-ed, I detail how winning the AI race against China is critical to the America First movement and protecting our most important resource: the American people. 
Read the full op-ed here. https://t.co/HeHSjAFlXv

Thank you to @CapitalYRs for hosting a phenomenal event last night! Always a pleasure to speak with the next generation of conservative leaders. We've lived through some of the most consequential times in decades, and now it's our job to lead on AI, make homeownership possible again, and rein in the national debt.

I want to make sure that we are outpacing our number one adversary in China. They are nipping at our heels, and so we have to beat China and the AI race. I want to make sure that we're protecting American workers. And so making sure that we thread the needle and that we have thoughtful leadership when it comes to artificial intelligence.
I think if these data centers are going to increase the burden on the community, they should foot the bill for that.

Among my legislative priorities are artificial intelligence. This is a seismic technology that is really changing the fabric of culture, society, our nation, and it is going to change the world. We need to make sure that we're outpacing China, but we also need to make sure we're protecting our kids' online safety. We need to make sure we're protecting American workers, the dignity of the human person, and we need thoughtful leaders in the AI space.
